title: gpu-kernel-stall-heatmap-scheduling-jul-2025
content:
Summary:

Short-running exploratory run profiling recent regression in per-token latency for the chat generation path. Goal was to map where GPU cycles are being wasted (stalls / low SM utilization) and determine whether CUDA Graph capture + persistent kernel strategy helps. This doc captures Nsight captures (Systems + Compute), heatmap-style timelines, and initial hypotheses + quick experiments.

Environment:
- Cluster: staging-dedicated-a100-1 (A100-40GB)
- Driver: 535.86.05, CUDA 12.2
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@v2.14.0-rc3 (custom compile with cublasLt, no MIG)
- Workload: chat generation, batch=1 per connection, seq_in=64, seq_out=256, top-p sampling (temp=0.8)
- Hot kernel observed: attn_kv_update, fused_mha_forward, kv_cache_write

Capture summary (what we recorded):
- Nsight Systems capture (nsys) of a 30s steady-state period with ~120 tokens generated across 6 concurrent streams. Captured host traces, CUDA API, memcpy, and CUDA kernel timeline.
- Nsight Compute for targeted kernel hotpath (fused_mha_forward) with metrics: achieved_occupancy, sm_efficiency, issue_slot_utilization, l2_hit_rate, dram_throughput, active_warps_per_sm, stalled_warp_avg.
- CUDA Graph capture attempt (cudaGraphLaunch) toggled on/off for same trace window to compare short-lived kernel launch overheads.

Key observations (timeline / heatmap analysis):
1) Inter-kernel gaps: Nsight timeline shows repeated 200-600us gaps between small kernels (kv_cache_write, small_reduction) that are host-driven and serializing on the default stream. These gaps add up (~15-40ms per second of token generation).
2) Low occupancy for fused_mha_forward under short sequence lengths: achieved_occupancy ~0.22 (22%) when seq_len=64, active_warps_per_sm ~8/64. SM efficiency reported ~31%.
3) Memory-bound stalls on kv_cache_write: stalled_warp_reason dominated by 'memory_throttle' and 'backend' stalls; DRAM throughput is spiky with low L2 hit rate (~12%).
4) Some kernels show high issue_slot_utilization but low warp occupancy (i.e., the warps that are active keep the issue slots busy but there aren't enough warps to hide latency).
5) CUDA Graph reduced host-side gaps by ~60% for the micro-batch launching pattern, but did not materially change SM occupancy for fused kernels. Total end-to-end per-token latency improved by ~8-12% in the capture window.

Quick hypotheses / root-cause candidates:
- Short sequence lengths -> insufficient parallelism per kernel, leads to low occupancy. Solution vector: kernel tiling or merging tokens across parallel contexts (batching) or persistent-thread kernels.
- Host serialization due to default stream + synchronous cpu work (scheduling, small memcpys) causing inter-kernel gaps. Solution: split streams, use async memcpys, pipeline on host, or cudaGraph to fuse launches.
- KV cache write is memory-bound because the cache layout causes scattered writes crossing L2 boundaries. Solution: re-layout KV cache to contiguous per-SM-friendly blocks or use coalesced writes and increase L2 locality (pack smaller types).
- Excess shared memory usage in the fused_mha kernel prevents higher block occupancy. Solution: reduce shared memory per block or split into multiple smaller kernels.

Experiment log (commands + notes):
1) Baseline system capture: nsys profile --output=prof_baseline --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn,osrt ./serve --config=staging
2) Targeted compute metrics: ncu --target-processes all --metrics sm__warps_active.avg,sm__warps_launched.avg,achieved_occupancy,sm__cycles_active.avg,issue_slot_utilization ./serve --args ...
3) CUDA Graph toggle: runtime flag --use-cudagraphs=(off/on) with identical input traffic.
4) Small memcopy detection: inserted nvtx markers around memcpy calls and compared host timelines in Nsight.

Detailed findings (per-kernel):
- fused_mha_forward:
  * achieved_occupancy: 0.22 (seq=64), 0.71 (seq=1024)
  * sm_efficiency: 31% (seq=64)
  * issue_slot_utilization: 85% when active
  * shared_mem_per_block: 48KB (experimentally measured via kernel attributes)
  Interpretation: kernel is compute-dense when warps are active, but there are too few warps per SM at short seqs. The shared memory footprint prevents increasing block concurrency.

- kv_cache_write:
  * avg_stalled_warps_reason: memory_throttle (65%), backend (20%)
  * dram_bw_peaks: ~70 GB/s during writes, sustained ~24 GB/s
  * l2_hit_rate: 12%
  Interpretation: writes are not cache-friendly; likely strided and small writes per thread.

- small_reduction & softmax_small:
  * frequent small kernels (~50–200 us) that serialize on stream0; combined they account for ~18% of wall-clock time due to host serial launching.

Cross-cutting signal: host-side scheduling/streaming is a large contributor to apparent GPU idle time. Even when kernels don't saturate the SMs, the host gaps are non-trivial at our target latency SLO.

Recommended tactical next steps (low friction):
- Short-term (1–2 weeks):
  1) Enable cudaGraph for the entire token generation pipeline in a staged A/B (already prototyped): quantifiable win ~10% latency. Rollout plan: feature flag per-model. Owner: Liam.
  2) Move small reductions and softmax_small to a dedicated high-priority stream and use cudaMemcpyAsync/streams to overlap host copies. Owner: Marcus.
  3) Add instrumentation NVTX + lightweight telemetry to record inter-kernel host gaps in production traces. Owner: Asha.

- Mid-term (2–6 weeks):
  1) Prototype persistent-thread variant of fused_mha to increase warp occupancy for seq<=128. Measure occupancy, SM efficiency, and power draw. Owner: Eng-MHA subteam.
  2) Layout change for KV cache: pack values to 16B aligned contiguous blocks and benchmark l2 hit rate / write throughput. Owner: Eng-KV team.

- Long-term (quarter+):
  1) Adaptive kernel launcher: runtime that chooses between persistent kernel (low-latency short seq) vs tiled kernel (long seq high throughput) at request time.
  2) Consider model compilation pass to split or fuse kernels automatically based on per-user sequence distribution.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Are there other customers running with seq~64 in prod? Need telemetry to validate distribution. (Linked to JIRA-INF-2412)
- Validate CUDA Graph memory usage regression risk for models that mutate states across launches. We saw one edge-case with pinned buffers; need test harness.
- Explore whether tensor core usage in fused_mha could be increased to reduce cycles and increase occupancy trade-off.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets:
- nsys collect: nsys profile --output out.nsys --trace=cuda,cublas --sample=none -- ./serve --workload tokengen
- ncu metrics capture: ncu --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm__warps_active.avg,sm__inst_executed_per_inst_slot_avg ./serve --args ...
- simple host gap calc (python pseudo):
  * parse nsys timeline events, compute delta between kernel end and next kernel start on the same stream, aggregate percent of time in gaps.

Notes / follow-ups from 2025-07-15 sync:
- Marcus ran the cudaGraph A/B overnight and confirmed 9–11% improvement tail p95 for single-connection throughput. No memory leaks observed in 12h run.
- Liam will add feature flag and rollout gate to Console for model-level opt-in.
- Next profiling target: persistent-thread prototype for fused_mha; aim for capture window by 2025-07-24.

Attachments / pointers:
- Raw captures stored: gs://staging-profile-dumps/2025-07/gpu-kernel-heatmap-ashakapoor-2025-07-10/{nsys, ncu}
- Confluence note (playbook): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/GPU+profiling+playbook

Status: draft — collecting results from persistent-thread experiment before promoting to in_review.
